items.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...they’ll get Ron Carter and people of that talent level to play behind them.

ctx.x: It’s always a tricky thing because with jazz there’s a lot of instances where it’s borderline. Is Rosemary Clooney a jazz singer? Well she sings jazz tunes and she swings. But does she improvise much? You know one could debate about that. And of course one always debates about Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett. Are they really jazz singers? Well sort of and sort of not. You know. Where someone like Kurt Elling or Betty Carter or Mel Torme, they’re definitely jazz singers. So I mean the quality that is needed is that…

Yeah there’s been a number of singers over the years who have come out with the debut album and I don’t know if it’s their choice or the record companies and they’ll get Ron Carter and people of that talent level to play behind them. And when you listen to it you say well it’s a jazz trio but it’s not really a jazz singer.

Like I say, it’s tricky. [inaudible] different singers much of the time but they might not sing jazz a hundred percent of the time. You just have to look at their overall career and then they are good musicians but they’re just singing straight. Generally if the singer does the song the same way one month to another they’re probably not a jazz singer. I mean with someone like Tony Bennett, he’ll perform a song and he’ll sing a chorus straight, then there’ll be half a chorus of sidemen playing, and then he comes…
